in_hebrew.name: איסידורוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם איסידורוס מקורו ביוונית ומשמעותו מתנה של אלוהים. הוא מורכב משני מילים: 'איסוס' שפירושו שווה ו-'דורוס' שפירושו מתנה. השם משמש כזכר ונקשר למסורת הנוצרית.

in_greek.name: Ισίδωρος
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ισίδωρος προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'ίσος' που σημαίνει ίσος και 'δωρος' που σημαίνει δώρο. Στη χριστιανική παράδοση, το όνομα αυτό συμβολίζει το δώρο του Θεού. Ο Ισίδωρος ήταν ένας σεβάσμιος άγιος και επιστήμων της Εκκλησίας.

in_latin.name: Isidorus
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Isidorus is derived from the Greek words 'isos' meaning equal and 'doros' meaning gift. In Christian tradition, Isidorus signifies a gift from God. The name was popularized by Saint Isidore of Seville, a revered scholar and theologian of the early Christian church.

data.cultural_impact: The name Isidorus was revered in the Middle Ages, particularly in the Iberian peninsula. Saint Isidore of Seville, a prominent scribe, writer, and bishop during that time, is the most famous bearer of this name. He was considered the 'last Scholar of the Ancient World' and is honored as a father of the Spanish Church. The name, therefore, came to symbolize wisdom, knowledge, and spiritual enlightenment.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian faith, the name Isidorus signifies God's gift and divine guidance. The name is believed to have been given by the Almighty Himself, hinting at the bearer's special connection with the divine. It reminds the believer of God's blessings and encourages them to continually seek knowledge, understanding, and wisdom from their faith.

historical_references.reference: Isidorus of Seville (c. 560-636 AD) was a prominent bishop and historian during the Visigothic Kingdom in Hispania (modern-day Spain). He is best known for his monumental work, the 'Etymologies' or 'Origins of Things', which was a comprehensive encyclopedia of the time.

Saint Isidore of Seville (560-636 AD) was a bishop in the early medieval Christian Church, particularly known for his role in the development of the Scholastic philosophy. He was a prolific writer and commentator on the works of the Church Fathers.
